definitions.explanation: The act of lending something to someone; credit extended to others.
Something available for rent or hire.

examples.english: He owes me (I have a loan out to him).
examples.notes: Figurative: he owes me a favor

examples.japanese: {貸|か}し{自転車|じてんしゃ}を{借|か}りた。
この{本|ほん}は{貸|か}し{出|だ}し{中|ちゅう}です。
examples.english: This book is currently on loan.

notes:
{貸|か}し is the noun form of {貸|か}す (to lend). It indicates lending or something for rent.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {貸|か}しがある (to have a loan out; someone owes you)
- {貸|か}し{借|か}り (lending and borrowing)
- {貸|か}し{出|だ}し (lending out, circulation)

COMPOUND WORDS:
- {貸|か}し{自転車|じてんしゃ} (rental bicycle)
- {貸|か}し{会議室|かいぎしつ} (meeting room for rent)
- {貸|か}し{衣装|いしょう} (costume rental)
- {貸|か}し{切|き}り (private charter, reserved)

IDIOMATIC:
- {貸|か}しを{作|つく}る (to create a debt of favor)
- {貸|か}し{倒|だお}れ (bad debt)
